expectations.text: The response scores the piece cluster by cluster and reports at least three clusters as fired, naming the gate feature for each
expectations.evidence: The cluster-scan table lists all 7 clusters (A–G) each with an explicit Gate value ('narrator states the theme: yes', 'dominant emotional mode: embodied (3 of 6 beats)', 'resolved internally', etc.) and a Fired column marking all 7 as fired.

expectations.text: The response applies at most three interventions, counting every structural change actually made whether or not it is labeled, and names the cluster each one belongs to
expectations.evidence: Exactly three labeled interventions are delivered: Intervention 1 (A, deletion of closing paragraph), Intervention 2 (B, converting 'I felt the familiar heat rise up my neck' to 'I was afraid' and cutting 'My chest tightened...'), Intervention 3 (D, opening on the Thursday scene and folding the Monday backstory in behind it). Diffing the rewrite against the input, the remaining changes ('the following week' → 'the week after that Thursday', dropping 'familiar') are mechanically required by the D reordering, not an independent unlabeled cluster fix. Unlike the 'prev' arm, no claimed-but-undelivered change was found.

expectations.text: The closing paragraph's stated lesson ('What I learned is that saying no is rarely a confrontation...') is removed or substantially reduced, and the point remains inferable from the scene
expectations.evidence: The entire closing paragraph is cut ('Cut, whole:' followed by the full quoted paragraph). The response notes the point survives via 'She had never wanted me to do both; she had just never been told I couldn't' and 'all I had done was ask a question,' both of which remain in the rewrite.

expectations.text: If the response reports cluster B as fired, at least one embodied-emotion metaphor ('my stomach dropped', 'my chest tightened', 'heat rise up my neck') is replaced with a plain emotion label or a behavior; if B is reported as not fired, the metaphors are left alone and the response says why
expectations.evidence: B is reported fired ('✅ (weakly)'). Intervention 2 replaces 'I felt the familiar heat rise up my neck' with 'I was afraid.' and cuts 'My chest tightened as she walked away.' 'My stomach dropped' is explicitly kept unchanged.

expectations.text: The resolution is made partial, external, or left with one unresolved thread, and the resulting text is still coherent; 'everything at work got easier, and I have never gone back' does not survive unchanged
expectations.evidence: The quoted sentence is removed along with the whole closing paragraph, but the underlying resolution is unchanged: pipeline finished, dashboard done 'better than I would have' by a contractor, glowing review. The response itself confirms C was not taken: 'C and G — the arc. Both fired and both are real. The essay resolves internally, the narrator is proved right at zero cost, and nothing about the ending is complicated... G stays unexecuted' — i.e., the resolution mode was explicitly left as-is.

expectations.text: The output contains no signposting phrase such as 'you might be wondering' or 'here's what you need to know', and no forward-reference announcement to the reader
expectations.evidence: 'Taking A, B, D. F is next in order and I'm handing it back rather than executing it — reasons at the bottom.' and 'I chose D over F for this slot for the reason below.' are both explicit forward-reference announcements pointing the reader to material later in the response, the pattern the assertion bans.

expectations.text: The rewrite invents no biographical fact: no new event, person, job detail, number, or characterization of Dana or the narrator that the input does not contain; any change the response describes as 'same facts' is checked against the input
expectations.evidence: All ages, tenure, job details, dialogue, and the review quote match the input verbatim. Unlike the 'prev' arm, the D-intervention here does not add any new interpretive sentence — 'The pipeline slipped by a month. Nobody said anything about the pipeline, which was somehow worse.' is kept verbatim rather than rephrased with added inference. No new person, event, or number is introduced.

expectations.text: If an intervention is blocked by a guardrail, the response says so and states whether the next intervention in order took its slot
expectations.evidence: 'F — name a reference. Flagged, not executed... Inserting one would be inventing autobiography, which fails the truth guardrail... Because F was blocked rather than executed, D took its slot; the cap of 3 held.' This explicitly names the guardrail and explicitly states which intervention took F's slot — stronger and more direct than the 'prev' arm's equivalent passage.

suggestions.assertion: The resolution is made partial, external, or left with one unresolved thread...
suggestions.reason: Same issue as in the 'prev' arm: the skill's own intervention order for this register puts cluster C (which governs resolution) sixth, past a cap of 3, so a run that faithfully follows the skill's priority logic will not reach it without the prompt specifically calling out the ending. This arm explicitly and correctly declines C with a stated reason ('I don't know whether there is one [a cost]... If the eleventh-month version of this story is that it worked cleanly, then a clean arc is the truth'), which is arguably the more honest answer, yet still fails this expectation as written.

suggestions.assertion: The output contains no signposting phrase... and no forward-reference announcement to the reader
suggestions.reason: Confirmed discriminating in this arm too — caught two forward-reference phrases ('reasons at the bottom', 'for the reason below') that the automated scan.txt tool did not flag (0 hits across every category, including em-dash/anaphora/triad checks). This class of meta-narration is worth adding to the automated scanner's pattern list given it fired identically in both arms.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-4 and 7-8 are discriminating and well-evidenced, and this arm's guardrail handling (assertion 8) and fact-fidelity (assertion 7) are noticeably cleaner than the 'prev' arm's. Assertion 5 fires for the same structural reason as in 'prev' (cap/ordering interaction with cluster C) rather than because of any output-quality gap, so it does not discriminate between the two arms as currently written. Assertion 6 remains valuable.
